problem: Rising pore pressure lowers the effective stress until the ground yields, the mechanism of injection- and rainfall-induced failure. In a laterally confined layer the yield pressure at each depth is exact, so a yield front moving down can be compared element by element.
result: On the 0.025 m mesh with 6400 steps every element yields within 0.23% (mean 0.15%) of its exact pressure, and 96 of 160 elements yield, as predicted. DES always yields slightly late; the delay falls with both the step and the mesh.
scope: 2D plane strain, uniaxial strain, elastic–perfectly plastic Mohr–Coulomb without dilation, fully saturated. Before yield the DES effective stresses follow the exact path within 0.05%, so the remaining error is the onset itself: it is read at the first saved step with plastic strain (up to one load increment late) and carries the one-step lag of the sequential coupling; both shrink with the step, and a spatial part with the mesh. Mean errors: 0.2 m, 400 steps: 1.25%; 0.1 m, 400 steps: 0.90%; 0.05 m, 400 steps: 0.70%; 0.05 m, 1600 steps: 0.35%; 0.05 m, 6400 steps: 0.28%; 0.025 m, 1600 steps: 0.23%; 0.025 m, 6400 steps: 0.15%. With PT option 1 instead of 0 (0.05 m, 1600 steps) the mean error is 0.351% against 0.354%. 3D: the first elements yield within 0.33%, but PT then stalls on the Mohr–Coulomb edge of equal horizontal stresses; queued for a larger machine. (a) yield front; (b) stress paths; (c) error.
meaning: This checks effective-stress plasticity in a boundary-value problem driven by pore pressure: the Biot coefficient in the effective stress, the Mohr–Coulomb return and the pressure coupling together.
